# Collections

robjc has three families of collections that hold `RSObject` instances.
Each family has a read-only class and a mutable class.
Choose a family based on how you need to find elements, and choose a class based on whether you need to change the elements or their order.

| Family | Read-only | Mutable | Main property |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Array | `RSArray` | `RSMutableArray` | Ordered; indices start at 1 |
| Dictionary | `RSDictionary` | `RSMutableDictionary` | Looks up values by key |
| Set | `RSSet` | `RSMutableSet` | Removes duplicates; order is undefined |

A read-only collection cannot be modified.
Its `copy()` returns the same instance, while `mutableCopy()` creates an editable collection.
For a mutable collection, `copy()` creates a separate read-only instance and `mutableCopy()` creates a separate mutable instance.
These copies are shallow, so they may share the objects they contain.

## Array: access by position

An Array stores robjc objects in order.
As in R, indices passed to `objectAtIndex()` start at 1.
A mutable Array lets you add, insert, replace, and remove elements.

```{r}
library(robjc)

array <- RSArray_withObjects(list(
  RSString_withValue("first"),
  RSString_withValue("second")
))
stopifnot(identical(array$objectAtIndex(2L)$value(), "second"))

editable_array <- array$mutableCopy()
editable_array$addObject(RSString_withValue("third"))
stopifnot(identical(array$count(), 2L))
stopifnot(identical(editable_array$count(), 3L))
```

`asList()` returns the stored objects as an ordinary R list.
An Array preserves both element order and duplicates.

## Dictionary: look up values by key

A Dictionary associates robjc keys with values.
Use `objectForKey()` to retrieve a value and `containsKey()` to check whether a key exists.
Lookup uses `hash()` and `isEqual()`, so an equal key can retrieve a value even when it is a different object from the key used at insertion.
For a custom key class, pass the calculated hash through `robjc_normalize_hash()` before returning it to avoid `NA_integer_`.

```{r}
dictionary <- RSDictionary_withObjectForKey(
  RSNumber_withValue(10L),
  RSString_withValue("id")
)
stopifnot(dictionary$containsKey(RSString_withValue("id")))
stopifnot(identical(
  dictionary$objectForKey(RSString_withValue("id"))$value(), 10L
))
```

Dictionary element order is undefined.
A key is copied with `copy()` when inserted; its hash and equality must remain stable while it is stored.
See the [equality and hashing guide](guide_08_Hash_isEqual.Rmd) for key stability.

## Set: unique elements

A Set keeps one representative of each group of equal elements.
Its iteration order is undefined.
Membership checks use each object's `hash()` and `isEqual()`.
A mutable Set lets you add and remove elements. `uniteSet()`, `intersectSet()`, and `subtractSet()` return new read-only Sets.
A custom element class should also return the result of `robjc_normalize_hash()` at the end of its `hash()` method.

```{r}
set <- RSSet_withObjects(list(
  RSString_withValue("a"),
  RSString_withValue("a"),
  RSString_withValue("b")
))
stopifnot(set$count() == 2)
stopifnot(set$containsObject(RSString_withValue("a")))

editable_set <- set$mutableCopy()
editable_set$addObject(RSString_withValue("c"))
stopifnot(set$count() == 2)
stopifnot(editable_set$count() == 3)
```

A Set retains inserted objects without copying them.
While an object is stored in a Set, do not change state that determines its hash or equality.
To store a null value in a Set or Dictionary, pass `RSNull$null` explicitly.
Passing R's `NULL` directly is an error.
